sentences.text: The Jamaican ibis, scientifically named Xenicibis xympithecus, is an extinct bird species uniquely characterized by its club-like wings.
Based on a maximum femur diameter of 8.7 mm, the bird is estimated to have weighed about 2 kg.
This specific wing adaptation seems unique among all known birds.
Flightlessness was confirmed after a humerus was found in Swansea Cave, Jamaica, following an initial presumption based on an incomplete coracoid.
Fossils from locations including the Red Hills Fissure show a unique modification of the carpometacarpus that rendered the wing club-like.
Ornithologists speculate the wings were used as weapons like a club or flail, similar to adaptations in mantis shrimps.
The species belongs to the order Pelecaniformes, family Threskiornithidae, and subfamily Threskiornithinae.
The Jamaican ibis was endemic to Jamaica.
The species lived during the Holocene, from 0.0117 to 0 million years ago.
Fossils from Cuba once claimed to belong to this genus were later identified as belonging to a limpkin.
